extraction.input_text: On the issue of whether Daniel drove negligently, the fact that Daniel testified during the trial that he told his wife he was tired before driving into a tree.

claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The statement 'I was tired' was made prior to the trial, satisfying the out-of-court requirement of FRE 801(c).
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires the statement to be made by the declarant on a different occasion.
arguments.evidence_span: Daniel testified during the trial that he told his wife he was tired before driving into a tree.

arguments.text: The statement 'I was tired' constitutes an assertion of fact regarding Daniel's physical condition.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires the statement to be an assertion.
arguments.evidence_span: he told his wife he was tired

arguments.text: The statement is offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted (that Daniel was tired) to establish negligence.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires the statement to be offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of whether Daniel drove negligently, the fact that Daniel testified during the trial that he told his wife he was tired before driving into a tree.

arguments.text: Daniel is a party to the litigation, so the statement may qualify as a party-opponent admission under FRE 801(d)(2), excluding it from hearsay.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(d)(2) excludes party-opponent admissions from the definition of hearsay.
